prompt: Complete the generic methods on Maximizer: max returns the largest element of a list by natural ordering (null for an empty list), and lastOrDefault returns the last element or a fallback.
explanation: The bounded type parameter <T extends Comparable<T>> guarantees every element has compareTo, so one implementation of max serves Integer, String, and any other Comparable type. Starting the best-so-far variable at null makes the empty-list result fall out naturally. lastOrDefault needs no bound at all because it never compares elements -- generics should demand only the capabilities a method actually uses.
hints: The bound <T extends Comparable<T>> is what lets max call compareTo on the elements.
Track a best-so-far variable that starts as null; any element beats null, and later elements must beat the current best.
In lastOrDefault, guard with items.isEmpty(); otherwise the last element sits at index items.size() - 1.
